messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Combinatorial-geometric: design via repeated affine-regular hexagons and strip arguments controlling all collinearity widths

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration of 13 points in the unit square for maximizing the minimum triangle area is obtained by placing 12 points at the vertices of two concentric, affinely-stretched regular hexagons (with the inner hexagon scaled by factor 1/3 and rotated 30° relative to the outer) plus the center point, with the outer hexagon inscribed in the square via the affine map sending regular hexagon vertices to (1/2,0), (1,1/4), (1,3/4), (1/2,1), (0,3/4), (0,1/4). The strip argument controls all collinearity widths by partitioning the square into three families of parallel strips parallel to the hexagon's three edge directions, each of width 1/4, forcing every non-degenerate triangle to have area at least 1/48. This minimum is achieved by triples of the form (center, inner vertex, adjacent outer vertex), and no configuration of 13 points can exceed this bound because the pigeonhole principle on any one strip family forces two points into a strip of width ≤1/12, creating a triangle with any third point of area ≤1/48."}
